topic: Why local AI evaluation loops matter more than model size
draft:
I've seen teams obsess over model size, only to hit dead ends in production.  

The real bottleneck isn't parameter count—it's the feedback loop between model behavior and data.  

In one AI project, we scaled a 10B parameter model, but the output was inconsistent. The issue? We weren't evaluating the model's behavior against real-world data in a local loop.  

Local evaluation loops let you catch drift, refine prompts, and debug edge cases before they hit users.  

Model size matters, but without a robust evaluation loop, you're just chasing hype.  

Build the loop first.
final_text:
I’ve seen teams spend a lot of time and resources scaling up model size, only to hit roadblocks when it comes to real-world use.  

The real problem isn’t how big the model is—it’s how well you’re understanding how it behaves in practice.  

In one project, we built a 10B parameter model, but the output was all over the place. The issue wasn’t the model itself—it was that we weren’t testing its behavior against real data in a local loop.  

A local evaluation loop helps you spot issues early, refine what the model is actually doing, and catch edge cases before they affect users.  

Model size matters, but without a solid way to measure and improve performance, you’re just chasing the latest trend.  

Start with the loop.
